formal_statement: ∀ k : ℕ, ∃ n₀ : ℕ, ∀ n : ℕ, n₀ ≤ n → ¬ ∃ (n' s : ℕ) (w : (Fin n → Bool) → List Bool) (T : (Fin n → Bool) → List Bool), 2 ^ n' ≤ n ^ k ∧ PEqualNP.MetaComplexity.QueryLocal n 1 w ∧ (∀ x : Fin n → Bool, w x = List.replicate s true ++ false :: T x ∧ (T x).length = 2 ^ n') ∧ ∀ x : Fin n → Bool, (Finset.univ.filter fun i : Fin n => x i = true).card % 2 = 1 ↔ w x ∈ PEqualNP.MetaComplexity.MCSP
plain_statement: CONJECTURE, OPEN, could be false: for every k and all large n, no 1-local map (every output bit fixed by one input bit, non-uniform) whose outputs are MCSP instances of one size bound s and tables of one length N <= n^k reduces parity on n bits to MCSP. A special case of a question open in print (is MCSP hard for parity under non-uniform projections; the 2021 gap paper, Section 7; printed opinion leans to hardness, which would refute this). Checked so far: near-linear N for partial tables (L-meta-049 with 044).
title: HARD LINK (open): no 1-local fixed-format reduction of parity to MCSP with truth tables of length polynomial in n
